props.title: That Darn Cat!
props.initialSlug: Clever cat leads FBI to solve a kidnapping caper

sections.content: Disney's foray into live-action comedy-mysteries hit its stride with That Darn Cat!, starring Hayley Mills and Dean Jones. The film perfectly balances family-friendly hijinks with legitimate suspense, establishing a template Disney would follow for decades. Like The Parent Trap (1961) and The Moon-Spinners (1964), it showcased Mills' remarkable ability to carry sophisticated plots while maintaining youthful charm. Director Robert Stevenson, who helmed Mary Poppins (1964), brings his signature touch of whimsy to what could have been a standard caper.

sections.content: The film marked a significant evolution in Disney's live-action offerings, moving beyond pure fantasy like Darby O'Gill and the Little People (1959) into more contemporary settings. Dean Jones would become Disney's go-to leading man through the 1960s and 70s, starring in hits like The Love Bug (1968) and The Shaggy D.A. (1976). The success of That Darn Cat! proved audiences would embrace family films that incorporated elements of adult genres like mystery and crime. SUBHEAD: The Disney Live-Action Formula Takes Shape

That Darn Cat! established several elements that would become hallmarks of Disney live-action films: a mix of slapstick and genuine tension, clever animal performers, and strong adult supporting casts. This blueprint influenced later successes like The Cat from Outer Space (1978) and Homeward Bound: The Incredible Journey (1993). The film's ability to appeal to both children and adults without talking down to either audience remains impressive.
